basis: Exact Chinese 0.11.24 source criteria; trial authorized on 2026-11-25. No new EC calibration.

EC-TIME.title: Reply timeliness
EC-TIME.passCriteria: Use only the source review time and first reply time. A continuous elapsed duration of at most 24 hours is PASS; exactly 24 hours is PASS. Include nights, weekends and holidays.
EC-TIME.failCriteria: A continuous elapsed duration strictly greater than 24 hours is FAIL. The same threshold applies to every site and review type. Uncertain or failed review classification does not block this check.
EC-TIME.exceptionCriteria: Return UNKNOWN if a reply exists but its first reply time is missing or invalid, the review time is missing or invalid, timestamps run backwards, or reply fields conflict. Never substitute the latest reply time, last reply time or a model estimate for the first reply time. If both reply text and first reply time are blank, measure the unreplied duration up to the frozen inspection cutoff and explicitly mark it as unreplied; this cutoff is not an inferred first reply time.

EC-TEXT.title: Text quality
EC-TEXT.passCriteria: Check spelling, grammar, punctuation/emojis and meaning individually. Count only significant errors that impair understanding, create material ambiguity or clearly damage professional presentation. PASS when the count is below the frozen semanticPolicy.text.minimumSignificantErrors threshold: one by default, or two if explicitly selected by the administrator.
EC-TEXT.failCriteria: FAIL when significant errors supported by reliable source evidence reach the frozen threshold. Quote each error and explain its effect on understanding, material ambiguity or professional presentation. A spelling difference alone is insufficient. Do not count the same error twice.
EC-TEXT.exceptionCriteria: Capitalization, minor spelling or punctuation, omitted accents, language variants and nonstandard words copied from the customer are advisory only when they do not impair understanding or professional presentation; mention them in reason without counting them as significant errors. Also mention significant errors below the threshold as advice. Return UNKNOWN if there is no public reply or the original language cannot be understood reliably; do not assume PASS.

EC-TARGET.title: Targeted response and batch repetition
EC-TARGET.passCriteria: For positive reviews, PASS if the reply addresses any specific praise point or adds information relevant to the actual review. Explicitly reflecting a specific praise point may PASS even with a formulaic sentence pattern; phrasing can be advisory. Additional product explanation, usage advice, personalized handling or follow-up is not mandatory. Generic thanks, wishes or isolated keywords do not address a specific praise point. For medium/negative reviews and negative concerns, PASS when the reply addresses the concrete issue or gives related progress, a solution or steps. An apology/acknowledgement plus an issue-specific explanation, clarification or account of the situation plus a usable official channel also passes; resolution already achieved, a detailed workflow and a promised deadline are not required. High ratings containing negative concerns follow the negative-concern boundary.
EC-TARGET.failCriteria: For positive reviews, the individual semantic check is FAIL only when the reply both addresses no specific praise point and provides no relevant additional information; both conditions must hold. Generic praise answered only with generic thanks, wishes or polite stock phrases still fails. Do not invent product facts or issues. For negative concerns, generic apology plus a contact channel, or repetition of issue keywords without an issue-specific explanation, clarification, situation or action, is FAIL. The batch repetition check fails only for at least three distinct source rows under the same nonempty administrator, with every pair of replies reaching 85% normalized character-bigram Dice similarity. Never combine administrators or propagate failure through a chain of merely adjacent similarities.
EC-TARGET.exceptionCriteria: When classification has completed as invalid, the individual EC-TARGET semantic/relevance subcheck is NA; do not penalize failure to address meaningless content. Do not infer an unfinished or failed classification. The batch repetition subcheck remains independent: semantic NA cannot override its FAIL. Missing original review or reply remains UNKNOWN. Only two similar replies by the same administrator are advisory, not an automatic batch failure. If the administrator is missing, do not guess ownership: mark the batch subcheck incomplete while retaining any individual semantic FAIL. WhatsApp, hotline or private-message channel words do not automatically cause FAIL. Assess channel usability only from the reply and frozen references, without external lookup or speculation. In reason, briefly identify the review points, the specific response/relevant added information, and what is met or missing. Separate advice from hard failure; add no required output fields. This release leaves the negative-concern boundary unchanged pending business arbitration.

EC-STEPS.title: Reply structure
EC-STEPS.passCriteria: When a reply contains at least three operation or troubleshooting steps, number every step in order; forms such as First step, circled numbers and 1. are accepted. Fewer than three steps are exempt. For positive high-rating reviews, opening + product value + closing, and for negative high-rating reviews, opening + apology + solution + closing, are writing suggestions only. Missing a fixed paragraph does not itself cause FAIL.
EC-STEPS.failCriteria: FAIL if at least three operational steps are not fully numbered in order, or if a positive/negative high-rating review receives an unrelated reply with no substantive response. Reasons must distinguish step numbering, substantive response and advisory paragraph structure. Missing an opening, separate product-value paragraph, apology or closing alone must not cause FAIL.
EC-STEPS.exceptionCriteria: Keep the existing structure criteria for medium/low ratings; do not apply the fixed high-rating paragraph pattern to them. Polite phrases are not operational steps. Incomplete high-rating paragraph structure is advice in reason only. Retain the existing Chinese/English visible-character counts and closing-waiver parameters. Return UNKNOWN when classification is unknown and the decision depends on it, the reply is absent or evidence is insufficient; do not assume PASS.

EC-PRIVACY.title: Public-reply compliance
EC-PRIVACY.passCriteria: The public reply discloses no personal information or sensitive/prohibited content. A customer name used solely as a polite form of address, such as Hi Sara, is permitted when no other personal information is disclosed alongside it.
EC-PRIVACY.failCriteria: FAIL if the public reply contains a telephone number, address, email, personally linkable order details or other personal information, or sensitive/prohibited content. Masked personal information is also prohibited. A name used beyond a simple greeting or disclosed with other personal information is outside the greeting exception. Quote the actual public-reply evidence.
EC-PRIVACY.exceptionCriteria: The name exception is limited to a polite greeting with no other personal information; it does not permit linking a name to orders or contact details. Personal information in the input spreadsheet alone is not public disclosure. Return UNKNOWN if there is no reply or it is unclear whether the content is personal information. Minor expression advice belongs in reason only.

referenceSections.source-row-21: III. Review reply strategies (reference content for AI assistance).
referenceSections.source-row-23: Scenario | Suggested reply time | Reference structure | Reference example.
referenceSections.source-row-24: Positive high-rating review | 24H | Opening + product value + closing. Example: Dear customer, thank you for recognizing and supporting our products (opening) + [product] offers [key benefits such as performance, battery life or design, reflecting the review] to make your experience convenient and enjoyable (product value) + We hope you enjoy exploring more products. Contact our store support whenever needed, and have a wonderful day (closing). This is reference writing guidance, not an independent rule or time override.
referenceSections.source-row-25: Negative high-rating review | Opening + apology + solution + closing. Example: Dear Huawei customer (opening), we are sorry for the disappointing experience (apology), [solution], and thank you for your support. Please contact store support if you need further help; have a pleasant day (closing).
referenceSections.source-row-29: Positive high-rating strategy: (1) Opening may greet, thank, acknowledge or compliment the customer. (2) Product-related content may concern product benefits or store service. If the review mentions one or several benefits, respond to one of them, for example image quality when the customer praises pixels. If no benefit is mentioned, choose a relevant product benefit or store service. (3) Closing may offer wishes, thanks, acknowledgement or a service commitment. A closing may be omitted when the response is too long or the situation makes it inappropriate.
referenceSections.source-row-30: Negative high-rating and medium/low-rating strategies | Problem type | Scenario | Solution.
referenceSections.source-row-31: How-to enquiries | Questions such as how to operate the product | Give a targeted answer to the customer's operation question.
referenceSections.source-row-32: Fault-related problems | Product defects, appearance/structure, materials/workmanship, product information | Opening + solution + recommendation for inspection at a service store + closing.
referenceSections.source-row-33: Feature/appearance shortcomings | Problems with feature experience or cosmetic imperfections | First explain the product's actual support for the feature, then address the customer's specific concern.
referenceSections.source-row-34: After-sales problems | Returns/refunds, warranty/repair, invoices/documents and after-sales channel quality | Respond to the specific issue. Example: Regarding [the issue stated in your review], we have checked [verified circumstances]. If [condition], you can [specific solution].
referenceSections.source-row-35: Delivery problems | Transportation and delivery service | Respond to the specific issue. Example: We have confirmed that [the delivery problem stated in your review] is due to [verified cause], and have arranged [specific solution].
referenceSections.source-row-36: Price problems | Promotion rules, price changes or additional charges | Respond to the specific issue. Promotion rules: We are sorry for the inconvenience; the promotion rules are [rules]. Cross-platform comparison: Different platforms use different operating and promotional strategies and resources, which can lead to reasonable price differences. Store price changes: Thank you for your interest in Huawei; promotions may differ across periods.
referenceSections.source-row-37: User experience | No concrete issue but dissatisfaction, complaints about price or value | Illustrative product-benefit wording: HUAWEI WATCH FIT 5 has a slim and light design, weighing 27 g and measuring 9.5 mm thick, suitable for commuting and exercise. These source-example specifications are illustrative writing material, not a substitute for verified product knowledge.
referenceSections.source-row-38: Several issues in one review | Focus on one or two most important issues affecting use | Example: Regarding the issues you raised, our support team has [action] + at most two solutions + closing.
referenceSections.source-row-39: Excellent positive-reply guidance: (1) Connect the opening and closing or build meaningful interaction; references must relate to the body and the review. (2) Be warm, positive and approachable; avoid negative wording and use tact. (3) Be concise, coherent and easy for most readers to understand, without contradicting earlier content. (4) Use a fresh, engaging style without vulgar humor. (5) Match the review's content and tone, such as loyal Huawei users, formal business users, youthful/playful customers and product context; avoid a uniform stock reply. Practical checks: connection—does the reply refer to the review's keywords/emotion? Positive example: clear photos → mention imaging; negative example: clear photos → only thank you for your support. Warmth—use friendly language: glad you like it versus we received your review. Concision—three to five focused sentences versus a long response without a clear point. Style match—light language for a playful review versus internet slang in response to a formal customer. Source adoption note #26: add assessment methods and positive/negative examples for each requirement.
